nodes.process_description: This is an esterification reaction for the synthesis of Octocrylene, a UV filter commonly used in cosmetics and sunscreen formulations. Transesterification/Ester Exchange Reaction - The ethyl ester of Etocrylene is converted to the 2-ethylhexyl ester (Octocrylene) with ethanol as the byproduct. Temperature: 60-120°C. Pressure: Atmospheric to slightly elevated (0.5-2 bar), with potential vacuum application to drive off ethanol byproduct. Catalysts: Acid catalysts (titanium(IV) chloride, tin(II) chloride, or p-toluenesulfonic acid) at 0.1-1 wt%. Solvents: Process may operate neat or with toluene/xylene. Reaction time: 2-8 hours. Equipment: Batch or continuous reactor with temperature control, distillation column for ethanol removal, condenser for vapor recovery. Molar ratio: 1:1 or slight excess of 2-ethylhexanol (1:1.2-1.5). Workup: Ethanol removal via distillation under reduced pressure, catalyst neutralization with base, extraction and washing, crystallization for high purity. Industrial Applications: Large-scale cosmetic and personal care synthesis.

This reaction represents a deoxidative decarbonylation process converting a diol to a primary alcohol using carbon monoxide as a reducing agent. The reaction transforms 2-butylbutane-1,3-diol into 2-ethylhexan-1-ol by selective removal of one hydroxyl group via decarbonylation, with CO as the reducing agent and CO2 as a byproduct. Catalytic System: Transition metal catalysts required, likely rhodium (Rh) or similar platinum group metals. Catalyst loading: 0.5-5 mol%. Reaction Conditions: Temperature 100-150°C, Pressure 1-5 atm CO atmosphere, Solvent: Aromatic hydrocarbons (toluene, xylene) or ethers (THF, dioxane), Reaction time: 2-12 hours. CO handling requires specialized equipment with inert atmosphere/positive pressure control. Safety: CO is toxic and flammable; closed systems with proper ventilation essential. Selectivity: Selective reduction of secondary hydroxyl group over primary (steric factors). Industrial: Used for specialty alcohol production for plasticizers, detergents, and pharmaceutical intermediates.

This is an ester hydrolysis process, specifically the saponification/hydrolysis of ethyl 2-(1-hydroxyethyl)hexanoate to produce 2-(1-hydroxyethyl)hexanoic acid and ethanol. The ethyl ester group is cleaved by water, producing the free carboxylic acid and ethanol as byproduct. The hydroxyl group on the adjacent carbon is preserved. Temperature: 70-85°C optimal. Catalysts: Acid catalysis with H2SO4 or HCl at 0.5-2 wt% concentration. Solvent: Water (primary); aqueous ethanol mixture to improve miscibility. pH: 1-3 (strongly acidic). Pressure: Atmospheric or slight positive pressure. Reaction time: 2-6 hours. Equipment: Glass-lined or stainless steel reactor with mechanical stirring, temperature control system, condenser to recover ethanol vapors. Molar ratio: Water in excess (typical 10:1 or higher). Separation & Recovery: Ethanol recovered via distillation; product acid precipitates on cooling; extraction using organic solvent; acid-base extraction. Typical Yield: 90-98% based on starting ester.

This is a selective ketone reduction reaction converting ethyl 2-acetylhexanoate to ethyl 2-(1-hydroxyethyl)hexanoate through catalytic hydrogenation. The reaction selectively reduces the ketone functional group (acetyl group) to a secondary alcohol while preserving the ester group. Catalytic System: Heterogeneous metal catalysts such as Ni/C, Pd/C, or Pt/C. Alternative: Homogeneous catalysts like RuCl2(PPh3)3 or RANEY nickel. Catalyst Loading: Typically 5-10 wt%. Reaction Conditions: Temperature 50-150°C (controlled to prevent side reactions). Pressure: 1-50 bar H2. Solvent: Protic solvents (ethanol, methanol) or aprotic solvents (ethyl acetate, THF). Reaction Time: 2-12 hours. Selectivity: The ketone is kinetically more reactive than the ester, enabling selective reduction. Lower temperatures and milder pressures favor ketone selectivity. Equipment: Autoclave or pressure vessel rated for hydrogen. Gas-liquid contact system (stirred reactor with H2 sparger). Temperature control jacket. Hydrogen supply system with pressure regulation and safety relief. Typical yield: 90-98% under optimized conditions. Atom economy: 97.8% (excellent).

This is an alkylation reaction, specifically a nucleophilic substitution (SN2) of ethyl acetoacetate with butyl bromide - a classic example of the acetoacetic ester synthesis. Ethyl acetoacetate (β-ketoester) acts as a nucleophile through its active methylene group (CH2 between two electron-withdrawing carbonyls), attacking the primary alkyl halide (butyl bromide) to form a new C-C bond, displacing bromide as the leaving group. Base Catalyst: Strong base required - Sodium ethoxide (NaEt) or potassium carbonate (K2CO3) in aprotic solvents, or sodium hydride (NaH). Base: typically 1-2 molar equivalents. Solvent: Polar aprotic solvents essential - Ethanol (if using NaOEt) or DMSO preferred; N,N-Dimethylformamide (DMF) acceptable. Temperature: Room temperature to 60-80°C. Higher temperatures (50-80°C) accelerate reaction significantly. Exothermic reaction requires controlled addition. Reaction Time: 2-24 hours. Equipment: Round-bottom flask with stirring and reflux condenser, addition funnel for controlled alkyl halide addition, inert atmosphere. Product Yield: Typically 60-85% under optimized conditions. Industrial Applications: Used to synthesize methyl ketones and other organic synthons in pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturing.

This is a Knoevenagel condensation reaction between ethyl cyanoacetate and benzophenone to produce etocrylene (ethyl 2-cyano-3,3-diphenylprop-2-enoate), a UV-absorbing compound used in cosmetics and sunscreens. Base-catalyzed Knoevenagel condensation (aldol-type reaction). Catalysts: Primary - Weak organic bases (piperidine, pyrrolidine, or secondary amines) or inorganic bases (K2CO3, Cs2CO3, or NaOH at catalytic quantities). Alternative: DBU (1,8-diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene) or other organocatalysts. Solvents: Polar aprotic solvents preferred - DMF, DMSO, or DMA (for faster reaction). Alternative: Methanol, ethanol, or toluene depending on scale and process economics. Reaction Conditions: Temperature 25-80°C (room temperature to moderate heating). Pressure: Atmospheric to slightly elevated. Duration: 2-24 hours depending on catalyst strength and temperature. Stoichiometry: 1:1 molar ratio. Mechanism: Base abstracts α-hydrogen from ethyl cyanoacetate to form reactive carbanion, carbanion attacks carbonyl carbon of benzophenone, hydroxyl intermediate forms and undergoes dehydration to yield conjugated product. Equipment: Jacketed reactor with mechanical stirring, reflux condenser, thermometer, addition funnel. Workup & Purification: Water removal by azeotropic distillation or vacuum distillation, product crystallization or column chromatography separation. Final purification typically yields >95% pure etocrylene. Industrial Applications: Etocrylene is a key intermediate/active ingredient in UV-absorbing cosmetic formulations (SPF products).
